Revenue Acceleration and Further Signal on GenAI ROIC… As detailed below, continued acceleration and upside for each companies' key revenue metric (Ad revenue, Hyperscaler revenue, etc.) will be important for revisions and the multiple investors are willing to pay. Investors will want to see continued ROIC signal on the ramping capex. 2. ...In Particular as '27 Capex Estimates Seem to Be Headed Higher over the Course of '26: We are ~15% ahead of consensus on "big 4" hyperscaler '27 capex, and our estimates could have upward bias based on our colleagues' hardware and datacenter component checks (chips, memory, optical, energy, etc.) pointing to continued strong demand. While we do not expect any updates on '27 capex this earnings season, we expect '27 capex uncertainty, and debates on FCF floors and when we will reach peak capex to revenue levels (investment intensity) to continue to put ceilings on multiples this year. 3. What is the Status of the Consumer? Weakness not priced as of now. As of now, we have heard of some evidence of the branded ad markets becoming weaker in April. This will likely impact smaller, less proven ad platforms (SNAP, PINS, RDDT) more, but we are monitoring this closely and will be listening for color from the companies on the latest trends in macro demand.
4. Search Funnel Changes? GOOGL not pricing in any disruption risk and META not pricing in any MetaAI success. With MetaAI set to improve and ChatGPT's commercial products improving as well, we are highly focused on changes in consumer behavior in our recurring survey work (see here for latest).
We now turn to our key debates/takes around META, AMZN, GOOGL...
META: Remains Top Pick; Revenue Revisions, MetaAI Commercial Behavior and Headcount Cut Details Matter
1. Core Revenue Acceleration and Revisions: As detailed in Key Debates, MetaClaw and Why to Buy META Now, we see META's ability to deliver and guide to better than appreciated top-line growth as being important to 1) Showcasing the ROIC of its GPU/GenAI investments to its core and 2) Establish higher floors in EPS/FCF through this heavy investment period. We model 34%/28% y/y revenue growth in 1Q/2Q....and 28%/21% in '26/'27.
2. Muse Enabled MetaAI Commercial Behavior and API Clarity: As detailed in Meet Meta's Muse, with the release of Muse Spark, more advanced MetaAI adoption, and material evidence of commercial behavior will matter next. We believe Meta intends to release the new MetaAI to its family of apps in the weeks ahead and will be monitoring commercial behavior as a signal of further potential long-term revenue. We are also curious to hear from Meta about its intentions regarding API licensing as a further under-appreciated revenue stream.

These incremental costs put an even higher importance on revenue upside and clarity around Meta's reported headcount cuts, which as we have written here could add $1-$2 of EPS. Please let us know if interested in our interactive bottom up Meta hyperscaler spend build. Exhibit 3: Meta's new NBIS and CRWV hyperscale partnerships cause us to lower '27 EPS by 6%. AWS Acceleration To Durable 30%+ Growth: Like META, much focus remains on ROIC and in this case durably faster (30%+) AWS growth. We have written extensively about the strength of AWS's backlog (most recently here) and see the slope of AWS growth this year driven by data center capacity opening (see here). Note, we also continue to hear that AWS core CPU demand remains strong (where we believe they are less constrained). As such, we raise our AWS 1Q/'26 growth to 29%/31%...acknowledging that if more capacity comes online, growth could come faster. 2. AWS Profitability Staying Above 30%: It is also important AWS delivers healthy profitability through surging, lower margin AI demand (now at a $15bn run-rate, or ~10% of the business). We see AWS margins staying in the low-to-mid 30s this year with four supporting reasons: 1) Still strong growth of CPU/Graviton, which we believe is higher margin, 2) AMZN’s ongoing restructuring efforts (now totalling 30K company-wide white collar workers the past 6 months with potentially more to come per social media here), 3) AWS recent pricing increases in EC2 as a tailwind to revenue and margins (here) and 4) Our modeling of AWS D&A and non-D&A Opex (see Exhibit 5 ).

Healthy ~$350bn AWS Backlog Demonstrating Breadth Beyond Private LLM Labs: As detailed in Amazon.com Inc: 5 Takeaways from the AWS OpenAI Agreement, with the addition of the $100bn OAI business, we now see AMZN’s backlog reaching ~$350bn at the end of 1Q. We believe AWS has to print a backlog number in-line with us as this assumes the company adds the OpenAI business as well as ~$20bn of non-private LLM business in the quarter (vs. our estimate of ~ $19bn of gross business added on average the prior 4 quarters). In our view, growth outside of the leading frontier labs is important for investors' confidence in the breadth of the business. 4. Paint Path to $10-$11 of GAAP EPS in ‘27...As Accelerating AWS Offsets Fuel Headwinds, Retail Investment: We raise '26/'27 AWS growth 2%/2% (vs. prior) on stronger demand signals and now model 31%/33% '26/'27 y/y growth (vs. 29%/32% prior). In '26, this higher AWS growth offsets fuel headwinds (see our fuel model in Exhibit 6 ) and ~$4bn of incremental Retail investment this year (lower FBA fees, 1P price matching and quick commerce in International, and Leo in N.America). Note, in a downside scenario, we estimate rising fuel costs could drive as high as a ~$4bn headwind to our '26 shipping costs (even when factoring in offsetting N.America FBA fuel surcharges). That said, our base model only incorporates ~$600mn/$2bn of 1Q26/2Q26 fuel headwinds, as we assume the company can find offsets in 2H. Even through these macro headwinds, incremental Retail investment, our '26 EPS only falls -2% vs. prior to $8.1 and our '27 EPS of $10.4 is unchanged. Note, in '27 we believe investors would like/need to see ~$10.50 of EPS. Please let us know if interested in our AMZN fuel model. Morgan Stanley Research

Paid Search: Accelerating to High Teens+ Growth: We model paid search to accelerate again to 19% y/y reported growth and 16% ex-FX growth in 1Q. Checks remain constructive, SEO is increasingly pressured, ROAS and click-through rates are improving and we think GOOGL's runway for further improvements to Search is long (further data integration, Overviews, AI mode, agentic offerings, etc.). See here for a list of innovations to search. Durably faster paid search growth is the purest form of GOOGL GenAI ROIC and earnings power. 2. Google Cloud: 60% Y/Y Growth…with 50%+ Incremental Margins: Our backlog work (see here) showcased how Google Cloud can grow 60%+ this year… with GCP growing ~70% within the segment. Like AWS, remember that the slope of quarterly growth will be driven by data center capacity opening. Google Cloud’s incremental margins remain one of the standout numbers of our coverage, reaching 56% last quarter. This is due to multiple factors including revenue scaling across the asset base, a large 1P LLM-driven business with Gemini, Vertex AI, and TPUs. We expect this to continue and model Google Cloud margins to reach 36%/38% in ‘26/‘27…as Google Cloud grows to make up 31% of company-wide EBIT by ‘28. Stepping back, by ‘28 we expect Google Cloud to reach 26% market share relative to peers by '28, up from 19% share in '25. We also look for more color on GOOGL’s
